Use case / tech: Issues the dollar token USDe; ENA is governance on top.
Tokenomics, supply & unlocks: Circulating share 67% -> 89% (data sites changed what they count: 10B -> 13.4B); Oct 5 unlock (~1.4B investor tokens) is over; team's 1.6B locked, ~0.7%/month to March 2028; a listed holder owns ~1/5 of tokens and needs foundation consent to sell.
Team, backers & partners: Standard Chartered estimates; ether.fi launching a dollar token on Ethena reserves (>$300M deposits could move).
Adoption & on-chain data: USDe supply $4.8B (Sept +20%, then -2% after rewards ended; $15B in Oct 2025); fees ~$22M last month (+31%), ~$260M/yr but none reaches ENA; backing mostly lending (basis trade 18%); holder yield <5%.
Institutional / ETF flows & buybacks: Buyback starts only when USDe is at $7.5B (needs +56%); at $20B it would be ~8% of mcap/yr.
Leverage & derivatives: OI ~$390M = ~13% (moderate); funding ~8%; perps >4x spot.
Valuation vs peers / fundamentals: mcap ~$2.9B for a token that currently receives none of the fees.
Chart / relative-valuation setup: ENA/ETH must break resistance (+20-70% outperformance) or risk ~-70%; vs BTC more than doubled in 90d.
Narrative, catalysts & cycle position: Standard Chartered: USDe $40B by end-2028 and ENA 42c by year-end (he calls it optimistic).
Key risks: USDe supply shrank when rewards ended; ENA is 'much more risky than a direct investment in Ethereum'.
Thesis summary: Supply overhang is behind it; the price assumes USDe grows >50% soon. A 12-month position 'might make sense' at this level, but exit earlier if ENA/ETH is clearly rejected at resistance. USDe supply decides it.

Use case / tech: Largest DEX on Base (Coinbase's chain); merging with Velodrome into 'Aero' on Oct 21.
Tokenomics, supply & unlocks: Printing ~4.8M AERO/week (~12% p.a., ~$2.5 of new tokens per $1 of fees); new rule caps rewards per pool by expected revenue (reset every 48h), hard ceiling 20% p.a., team expects 8-12%; ~half of AERO locked.

Adoption & on-chain data: TVL ~$400M (up from $335M); team claims the two exchanges have ~17% of spot volume on their chains and could triple it (no data).
Institutional / ETF flows & buybacks: Coinbase auto-converts holdings in early Nov; private wallets must use an upgrade portal.
Leverage & derivatives: OI ~$172M = ~18% of mcap (record); funding at baseline; perps ~1.5x spot.
Valuation vs peers / fundamentals: mcap ~10x the yearly payouts to lockers (flat <$2M/week for 4 weeks).
Chart / relative-valuation setup: Vs altcoins lower highs and lows, at the upper end of the range: +15% to break resistance or risk a -74% type decline.
Narrative, catalysts & cycle position: Oct 21 launch; read the new supply on-chain right after.
Key risks: Good news mostly priced in; 'launch already slipped two times'; supply rule may only be 'a new name'.
Thesis summary: A printer that follows revenue is better than a fixed one, so he leans toward buying into the launch rather than betting against it, but the price near resistance with record OI leaves little room. The first week after launch settles it: new supply clearly below ~4M/week means the cap works.
